subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB391.md - CLOSED. 14.9.25.3 SR13 sends the Format-2 pairing question to 14.7.6, whose rule 2 reads 'In a MOVE statement, at least one of the data items is an elementary data item and the resulting move is valid according to the rules for the MOVE statement'. THE WHOLE OF THAT QUESTION IS NOW ASKED, THROUGH ONE ENTRY. The first half (landed earlier under this note) deleted CorrespondingBinder.CorrMoveValid, a second private partial copy of table 16 that had no alphabetic row or column, no national and no boolean sender row ('_ => false') and a receiver axis that was one boolean folding National and Boolean receivers into the 'Numeric, Numeric-edited' column; the drift test proved the copy disagreed with MoveTable16.Refusal on eight sender rows. The second half, recorded here as the PARTIAL residual, is now landed too: rule 2 says 'the rules for the MOVE statement', PLURAL, and 14.9.25.3 SR10 - the rule that routes to table 16 - governs only 'For all other cases not described in Syntax rules 8 and 9'. SR8 and SR9 were therefore part of rule 2's question and neither was asked. BOTH MEASURED WRONG ON THIS TREE AND BOTH FIXED: (a) SR8 - 'If identifier-1 references a data item described with usage binary-char, binary-short, binary-long, or binary-double, identifier-2 shall reference a numeric or numeric-edited item' - with 05 K USAGE BINARY-LONG in the sending group and 05 K PIC X(5) VALUE 'ZZZZZ' in the receiving group, MOVE CORRESPONDING formed the pair and left K2=[00000] while the identical DIRECT move was refused COBOL0819 by the same compiler; it now leaves K2=[ZZZZZ] and the numeric and numeric-edited receivers the rule names still pair (conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb391_corresponding_rule2_sr8_binary, with the written-MOVE contrast pinned by conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb391-move-binary-long-to-alphanumeric-written). (b) SR9 - 'If identifier-1 or identifier-2 references a variable-length group then these groups shall be compatible groups as specified in 8.5.1.12' - a variable-length-group namesake paired with an elementary one in either direction and the emitted implied MOVE asked for a whole-group character image the pair can never have, so the program reached the RUN TIME as NotImplementedCobolFeatureException where the written MOVE was refused COBOL1931; both directions are now silent non-selections and the compatible group x group namesake still descends and moves its members (conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb391_corresponding_rule2_sr9_varlen). THE SHAPE: MoveTable16.DataItemRefusal is the whole of 14.9.25.3's validity question over two DATA ITEMS, in SR order (SR8, then SR9, then SR10's table), and CorrRule2MoveValid is one call to it - so the next MOVE syntax rule reaches CORRESPONDING without an edit. SR8's item-keyed test is the ShapeRefusal(DataItem, Table16Operand) overload and the pre-existing ShapeRefusal(BoundOperand, Table16Operand) entry now DELEGATES to it, so the two askers are one body; SR9's relation moved out of StatementValidation.CheckVariableLengthMove into MoveTable16.VariableLengthRefusal, which keeps COBOL1931's framing at the MOVE statement and is read SILENTLY here, because rule 2 makes an invalid move a pair that does not correspond rather than a diagnostic. Rule 4's class exclusion stays in CorrEligible through ItemCategory.IsIndexMessageTagObjectOrPointer - table 16 ADMITS a pointer x pointer pair, so it is the only thing refusing one. ALL THREE VERBS PROVED: CorrEligible and the descent are shared by MOVE, ADD and SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING, so rule 4 lands on all three; SR8 and SR9 are MOVE syntax rules and 14.7.6 rule 3 ('both of the data items are numeric') already subsumes them for the two arithmetic verbs - measured: ADD/SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING leave the BINARY-LONG x PIC X(5) namesake unpaired before and after, and still pair BINARY-LONG x PIC 9(5) (42 added, 42 subtracted). Rules 1, 3, 5 and 6 and the sending/receiving designation were verified correct earlier under this note and are unchanged. The drift test CorrespondingRule2DriftTests carries a Binary-long and a Variable-length-group position for the two rules SR10 defers to, and was verified to FAIL 18 of 40 against the pre-fix filter. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/MoveTable16.cs#Refusal (kb/Work PB2076 moved Table 16 to the runtime as MoveValidity.Table16Refusal, which MoveTable16's chain (DataItemRefusal) asks)
